name: Anohni
label: Secretly Canadian
lede: ANOHNI sang over cassettes in after-hours bars, named her band for a woman she met days before that woman died, and won the Mercury Prize with an album that jumped 119 places on the UK chart in a week.

eras.title: From San Jose to after-hours New York
eras.text: Born in England and raised in Amsterdam and the Bay Area, ANOHNI lands in Manhattan at 19 and builds a stage out of after-hours bars and late-night theatre. The band's name will come from a woman she met once, days before that woman died.

years.h: Chichester to San Jose, by way of Amsterdam
years.p: Born in 1971, ANOHNI moves with her family to Amsterdam in 1977 and to the San Francisco Bay Area in 1981, settling in San Jose. She has said she saw her own reflection in Culture Club's Boy George.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, ANOHNI attended Lincoln High School in San Jose, studied music and was an avid record collector: OMD, Kate Bush, Culture Club, Alison Moyet and Marc and the Mambas are the names it lists.

Wikipedia says she recalled seeing "her reflection" in [[Boy George|2787bddf-6439-4c73-8162-5f4a1e5fa030]], who would sing on the second Johnsons album more than two decades later.

years.h: NYU's Experimental Theater Wing sends ANOHNI to Manhattan
years.p: She spends the early 1990s singing in after-hours bars and clubs over pre-recorded cassettes, and writing and directing late-night theatre.

years.h: Blacklips starts as a cabaret, with Johanna Constantine
years.p: ANOHNI and Constantine found a queer and trans cabaret-theatre in New York in 1992. Wikipedia lists the collective as Blacklips, later Blacklips Performance Cult.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the founding to 1992, with ANOHNI and Johanna Constantine as co-founders. The shows ran alongside ANOHNI's after-hours singing and late-night theatre.

years.big: "Marsha P. Johnson, for me, is Jesus as a girl."
years.src: The FADER: ANOHNI is building tiny fires in a world made of darkness · Wikipedia: Anohni and the Johnsons · Wikipedia: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross
years.h: ANOHNI meets Marsha P. Johnson at Pride and kisses her hand
years.p: ANOHNI told The FADER she thanked Johnson at Gay Pride in 1992. Johnson died days later, and "the Johnsons" honors her.
years.xp:
ANOHNI told The FADER that Johnson was considered a saint in her lifetime, panhandling on Christopher Street and giving the money away. Of the name she said, "All my work has had some relationship...to sacred ancestry."

Wikipedia says ANOHNI founded the Johnsons as an experimental theater group in 1995, named for Johnson. Thirty years on, Alvin Baltrop's photograph of Johnson is the cover of My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross.

years.h: A grant pays for The Birth of Anne Frank / The Ascension of Marsha P. Johnson
years.p: The New York Foundation for the Arts funds the piece, staged at Performance Space 122. ANOHNI then asks musicians to help her record songs written in the early 1990s.

eras.title: A chamber band finds its label
eras.text: A chamber band forms around ANOHNI's voice. The first records come out on Durtro, the label run by Current 93's David Tibet.

years.h: The first Antony and the Johnsons show happens inside a Basinski installation
years.p: The ensemble plays The Kitchen in 1997 as part of William Basinski's Life on Mars. Cellist [[Julia Kent|63733317-8113-413a-8b8b-7ef89cd1f50d]] and violinist [[Maxim Moston|ca7ff952-74b6-4379-bfbb-03c86e1720c9]] are listed as members from 1999.
years.xp: Wikipedia says ANOHNI founded the Johnsons as an experimental theater group in 1995, and that the musicians assembled in 1997, when they began giving concerts as Antony and the Johnsons.

years.h: A debut on Durtro, from the man behind Current 93
years.p: David Tibet heard a recording and offered to release it. The self-titled album comes out in 2000; the 2001 EP I Fell in Love with a Dead Boy adds covers of Angelo Badalamenti and Current 93 songs.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Tibet, the Current 93 musician, offered the release through his Durtro label after hearing the tape.

years.cap: Antony and the Johnsons at the Paradise, Boston, September 2003
years.h: Anohni sings backup for [[Lou Reed|9d1ebcfe-4c15-4d18-95d3-d919898638a1]] on the Animal Serenade tour
years.p: She sings on songs from Reed's The Raven. Years later she's in his Berlin band too, a friendship that shows up on the 2023 album.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Anohni joined Reed as a supporting vocalist from 2003. She sang backup, with Sharon Jones and a children's choir, in his first complete performance of Berlin at St Ann's Warehouse in December 2006, and again at the State Theatre in Sydney in January 2007.

eras.title: The record that jumps 119 places
eras.text: I Am a Bird Now wins the Mercury Prize and turns a small chamber-pop record into a national event. Lou Reed, Björk and Hercules and Love Affair all want that voice on their records.

years.src: Wikipedia: I Am a Bird Now
years.h: Lou Reed sings on I Am a Bird Now, and so does Boy George
years.p: Secretly Canadian releases it in North America and Rough Trade in Europe. The cover is Peter Hujar's photograph of Candy Darling on her deathbed.
years.xp:
Reed plays guitar and sings on "Fistful of Love" and Boy George appears on "You Are My Sister", according to Wikipedia. Rufus Wainwright and Devendra Banhart are also on it. "Hope There's Someone" is the first single, out June 7, and peaks at No. 44 in the UK.

Wikipedia lists Pitchfork's No. 5 album of 2005, and The Guardian later ranked it 40th on its list of the 100 best albums of the 21st century.

years.src: Wikipedia: I Am a Bird Now · Wikipedia: Anohni
yt: Hope There's Someone on Later... with Jools Holland
years.h: Antony and the Johnsons win the Mercury Prize
years.p: The week after, I Am a Bird Now climbs from No. 135 to No. 16 on the UK chart, which Wikipedia calls the biggest jump in the history of the prize.
years.xp:
Mojo also named it Album of the Year, per Wikipedia. Its song "Bird Gerhl" ended up on the soundtrack of V for Vendetta.

Wikipedia puts UK sales at 220,000 by September 2011, and about 350,000 copies worldwide, 73,000 of them in the US.

years.cap: ANOHNI on stage in Lillehammer, Norway
years.src: Wikipedia: Anohni · Wikipedia: Anohni and the Johnsons
yt: Hope There's Someone, live in Stockholm, 2006
years.h: Turning puts New York's underground women on screen
years.p: With filmmaker Charles Atlas, the band takes the live video portraits to Rome, London, Paris, Madrid and Braga. The Guardian gives it five stars.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes Turning as a series of concerts alongside live video portraits of 13 femme underground New York figures, first done in 2004 and restaged in 2006.

Wikipedia quotes the Guardian calling it "fragile, life affirming, and truly wonderful", and Le Monde headlining it a "Concert-manifeste transsexuel".

years.cap: ANOHNI with Björk, Radio City Music Hall, New York
years.h: Jamaica and Iceland sessions put ANOHNI on Björk's Volta
years.p: Two songs, "The Dull Flame of Desire" and "My Juvenile", make the 2007 album. ANOHNI duets with [[Björk|87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb]] in London, Reykjavik and New York.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the sessions to 2006. The two reunited on record in 2015, when ANOHNI sang on "Atom Dance" from Björk's Vulnicura.

years.h: ANOHNI sings "Blind" on [[Hercules and Love Affair|b62ecfe7-b2e6-4d40-b7d2-8f12d3f51ed6]]'s debut
years.p: She's on five tracks of the disco record, and Pitchfork votes "Blind" the best track of 2008. Entertainment Weekly ranks it No. 2 on its 10 Best Singles of 2008.
years.xp: ANOHNI would return to Hercules and Love Affair in June 2022 on In Amber, leading six tracks and co-writing them with Budgie, the drummer of Siouxsie and the Banshees.

years.h: Another World EP turns the eye outward
years.p: Five songs, out October 7, a bridge from I Am a Bird Now to the environmental turn of the next record.

eras.title: Orchestras, lasers, a festival of her own
eras.text: The subject widens from the self to the planet, and the stage widens to orchestras. The band plays symphony halls, Paris in a Givenchy costume, and a Southbank festival ANOHNI curates herself.

years.cap: Antony and the Johnsons at Coachella, April 2009
years.h: Nico Muhly arranges The Crying Light, and Europe sends it to No. 1
years.p: Mixed by Bryce Goggin, it tops the European Billboard chart, Wikipedia says. ANOHNI calls it a record about landscape and the future.
years.xp: Ann Powers of the LA Times called it "the most personal environmentalist statement possible" and, as music, "simply exquisite", Wikipedia reports.

years.h: Symphony halls, with lasers in Manchester
years.p: The Manchester International Festival staging uses lasers by Chris Levine. Summer dates follow with the Manchester Camerata, Opera Orchestra of Lyon, Metropole Orchestra and Montreux Jazz Festival Orchestra.
years.xp: Wikipedia adds the Roma Sinfonietta to the run. At Salle Pleyel in Paris, ANOHNI wore a Givenchy costume by Riccardo Tisci.

years.cap: Swanlights at the Melbourne Festival, ANOHNI with Boy George
years.src: Wikipedia: Anohni · Wikipedia: Anohni and the Johnsons
years.h: Swanlights arrives with a book of ANOHNI's own drawings
years.p: Abrams publishes the book edition, with her collages and photography by Don Felix Cervantes. ANOHNI plays Lincoln Center that month for the late dancer Kazuo Ohno.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the album to October 12, 2010, on Secretly Canadian and Rough Trade, with an EP, Thank You for Your Love, in late 2010. It says Stereogum ranked it No. 8 on its Top 50 Albums of the year.

years.cap: Antony and the Johnsons with the Heritage Orchestra
years.src: Wikipedia: Anohni · Wikipedia: Anohni and the Johnsons
years.h: Cut the World goes live with the Danish Radio Orchestra
years.p: The album includes a spoken piece, "Future Feminism". The video, directed by Nabil Elderkin, has Willem Dafoe, Carice van Houten and Marina Abramović.
years.xp: Wikipedia says "Future Feminism" elaborates a connection between feminism and ecology. The album comes out in August 2012.

years.h: ANOHNI curates Meltdown at the Southbank Centre
years.p: The bill runs from Laurie Anderson, Diamanda Galas and Marc Almond to Boy George and Lou Reed.
years.xp: Wikipedia's list of Meltdown curators and artists also names Buffy Sainte-Marie, CocoRosie, Elizabeth Fraser, Kim Cattrall, Matmos, Light Asylum, Hercules and Love Affair, Joey Arias, Hal Willner, Cyclobe and William Basinski, plus The Voluptuous Horror of Karen Black.

eras.title: ANOHNI, under her own name
eras.text: A last show with Lou Reed, then a name change, a hard electronic record and an Oscar nomination she isn't asked to sing at.

years.cap: Antony and the Johnsons at the Teatro Real, Madrid
years.h: ANOHNI sings "Candy Says" with Lou Reed at his last show
years.p: At Salle Pleyel in Paris, ANOHNI and the Johnsons play with Reed on March 6. It's his last performance before his death.
years.xp: Conversations with Reed before he died shaped "Sliver of Ice" on the 2023 album. Wikipedia quotes ANOHNI: "He was a hardcore kind of guy and these moments were transforming the way he was seeing things."

years.h: ANOHNI announces Hopelessness, her first record under that name
years.p: She had used the name in private for years. Oneohtrix Point Never and Hudson Mohawke co-produce.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the first single, "4 Degrees", follows on November 30, 2015. ANOHNI said she "had grown tired of grieving for humanity."

years.h: Hopelessness aims electronic pop at drones, surveillance and capital punishment
years.p: Wikipedia says it has some sharp teeth. "Drone Bomb Me" arrives with a Nabil Elderkin video starring Naomi Campbell.
years.xp:
Hudson Mohawke says ANOHNI worked hands-on in Pro Tools, arranging and editing. It was nominated for the 2016 Mercury Prize, and she was nominated for a Brit Award, both per Wikipedia. Metacritic gives it 83.

The Guardian's Tim Jonze called it "as profound a protest record as anyone has made in decades." The New York Times called the tour, where she performed with her face under a veil in front of lip-syncing women, punk and radical empathy.

years.h: "Manta Ray" is nominated for an Oscar, and ANOHNI isn't asked to sing
years.p: She is the first openly trans performer nominated for an Academy Award. Wikipedia says the Academy described her as cut for time, though she says she was never asked; she stayed home.
years.xp: ANOHNI wrote that singing about eco-cide "might not sell advertising space", per Wikipedia, and pointed to systems that give trans people diminished opportunities. "Manta Ray" was written with J. Ralph for the film Racing Extinction.

years.h: Paradise EP ends with a track for anyone who emails ANOHNI a sentence
years.p: Same producers as Hopelessness. The final track goes to people who send in a sentence or two about what they care about most.

eras.title: Back to the Johnsons, with ten years of songs
eras.text: ANOHNI returns to the band name and to a warmer sound, with a new producer and ten years of unreleased writing. The New Yorker names it its album of the year.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily: ANOHNI Turns Toward Hope
years.h: The Blacklips years get a compilation
years.p: Blacklips Bar: Androgyns and Deviants collects the collective's 1992-1995 work a few months ahead of the new album.
years.xp: Bandcamp Daily describes the compilation as documenting the group's work on AIDS and environmental decline.

years.h: May 16: ANOHNI and the Johnsons return with "It Must Change"
years.p: The New York Times says she seems to sing in the voice of Mother Earth. The video stars Munroe Bergdorf, and the single is the first from Jimmy Hogarth's new studio band.

q: Hopelessness is the most strategic record I've ever made.
years.src: Wikipedia: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross · Album of the Year: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross · The FADER: ANOHNI is building tiny fires in a world made of darkness · Bandcamp Daily: ANOHNI Turns Toward Hope
yt: ANOHNI and the Johnsons: Tiny Desk Concert
years.h: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross gets cut at three or four songs a day
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.7. Jimmy Hogarth co-produces; the cover is Alvin Baltrop's photograph of Marsha P. Johnson.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Hogarth and ANOHNI started in 2022 and recorded three or four songs a day over two weeks, with many vocals ANOHNI's first takes. The reference points were Nina Simone and Jimmy Scott. Metacritic gives it 88 from 17 reviews; Album of the Year lists Pitchfork at 87, which is its 8.7.

The FADER says Rough Trade recommended Hogarth, whose credits include Amy Winehouse and Tina Turner (per Bandcamp Daily), and that the songs draw on ten years of unreleased writing. ANOHNI told the FADER that Hopelessness "is the most strategic record I've ever made."
play: My Back Was a Bridge for You to Cross

years.src: Treble: Watch the new ANOHNI video for Why Am I Alive Now?
years.h: Hunter Schafer directs the video for "Why Am I Alive Now?"
years.p: Shot at an industrial complex above the Pacific. Schafer says she wanted to focus on finding sisterhood in a world that does nothing to help.
years.xp: The video came out two days before the album. A live playback on the Rebismusic YouTube channel on July 6 featured Anohni, a Q&A with Schafer and Nomi Ruiz.

years.h: The New Yorker names it album of the year
years.p: The New York Times puts it at No. 10, Mondo Sonoro at No. 5, and Pitchfork at No. 9.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band toured Europe and North America in 2024, and that the Chicago Tribune called the Chicago show courageous, vital and provocative.
